static_traits.name: Joanna
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, keeping a pug as a pet
static_traits.social_status: Having a few close friends, but Decreased confidence due to weight issues, reduced sharing and socializing
static_traits.medical_history: No previous similar weight problems; no serious physical illness; never received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, fairly logical, able to be aware of and describe emotions and thoughts, highly cooperative, positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Weight gain from frequent snacking during late-night study, which in turn affects self-esteem and overall well-being
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to find healthier stress management and coping mechanisms, reduce the weight gain caused by late-night extra meals, and improve self-esteem and overall well-being
growth_experiences: Several months ago the course load clearly intensified, and she began studying at night more frequently; almost every night when completing homework or papers she adds food because of stress and fatigue (such as chips, biscuits, pizza), and subsequently her weight increased, and self-esteem and interaction with friends were affected; she tried healthier snacks and setting limits, but still finds it hard to control night eating.

core_beliefs: I'm a failure at managing life

special_situations.event: When rushing a paper/studying alone late at night, feels tired and stressed, needing to stay awake and focused
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not keep studying at night, I cannot complete tasks; if I do not eat, I cannot stay awake and efficient
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses snacks (high-calorie food) to refresh and forcefully extend study time
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I must eat something to continue focusing on finishing homework

special_situations.event: When with friends or thinking of socializing, feeling unconfident after noticing weight gain
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not attractive enough or gain weight, they will look down on me/I am not worthy of acceptance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing socializing and sharing, keeping problems to oneself and not seeking help from friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I look terrible; they will think I lack self-discipline

special_situations.event: After studying at night, realizes they ate many high-calorie snacks and attends to weight changes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot control nighttime eating, it means I lack self-discipline and am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism, setting stricter eating restrictions (but finding them hard to maintain)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not disciplined enough; I have failed at managing my life

special_situations.event: When evaluating the pros and cons of studying at night, mainly focuses on weight gain and negative effects while ignoring the benefits of improved efficiency and a quiet environment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative consequences matter more than positive gains; positive factors are not worth considering
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Judging and deciding with the negative at the core, further Reinforcing self-negation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Studying at night will only make me fat; it is all bad

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and recognized, maintaining self-esteem and attractiveness while maintaining study efficiency and a sense of control
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being looked down on/Being rejected (because of weight gain and lack of self-discipline), fearing losing control over oneself and studies
defense_goal: Rationalizing nighttime snacks by emphasizing efficiency and necessity to reduce shame and Anxiety
Avoiding exposing vulnerability to friends to maintain superficial self-esteem and safety
Promotes self-control through self-criticism, trying to make up for 'out-of-control' eating behavior

object_relations.object_representation: May look down on himself; others or peers who have demands on appearance and self-discipline

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When facing urgent academic tasks or deadlines and needing to stay awake and efficient late at night
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that only by eating snacks can one maintain focus and complete tasks, otherwise one will fail
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a rationalizing tone, finding 'necessity' reasons for nighttime snacks, emphasizing efficiency and must-ness, downplaying negative effects; if questioned, using words like 'must, have to'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether to share weight concerns with friends/support systems or when thinking about exposing vulnerability socially
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes that once problems are exposed, one will be looked down on and embarrassed; best to bear it alone to avoid harm
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cautious, reserved tone; responding briefly and quickly Displacing the topic to studying and tasks, avoiding deeply expressing shame and vulnerability.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing the evidence of weight gain after nighttime eating and my own performance
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Linking self-worth directly to weight/self-discipline, attaching the negative label of 'failure' to oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Low tone, using self-blaming expressions (such as 'it is all because I am not capable'), Reinforcing self-criticism, magnifying faults, downplaying successes.

manifestations: Not sharing weight and self-esteem struggles with friends, tending to bear stress and nighttime habits alone
Reducing socializing and help-seeking out of fear of being judged
outcomes: Social withdrawal and Increased sense of alienation
Worsened shame and Anxiety, Further decline in self-esteem

manifestations: Feels difficulty choosing between nighttime study and healthy habits, experiencing the pressure of self-discipline and choice
Defines own behavioral boundaries with 'must'-type rules
outcomes: Reduced tolerance for experience, rigid behavioral choices

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: In language, often uses 'must/should' to describe the necessity of nighttime studying and eating
Defines self-worth by external efficiency standards, ignoring bodily and emotional needs

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not seeking support from friends, turning stress and Anxiety inward to handle alone
Digests pressure through nighttime snacking and self-criticism

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism, tying self-worth to weight and discipline
In socializing, cautious and restrained in expression for fear of image being judged

positive_force: Learning efficiency and focus are better in the nighttime environment
Positive attitude and willingness to try different strategies (recording thoughts, exploring alternatives)
Having a certain degree of self-awareness, able to identify the relationship between stress and eating
Has a few trustworthy friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Habitual link between nighttime studying, high-pressure situations triggering eating to stay alert
Self-reproach and negative labels (undisciplined, failure) leading to Impaired self-esteem
Overly focusing on the negative, ignoring positive information (mental filtering/negating the positive)
Reducing socializing and help-seeking due to shame, forming a closed loop that worsens Loneliness and stress

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive snacking during late-night study (prefers high-calorie snacks)
antecedent: Studying alone late at night or rushing a paper
A quiet nighttime environment with available snacks
target_behavior.core_reason: Treats eating as the main strategy for staying awake and focused, to relieve stress and fatigue and help complete academic tasks
target_behavior.function: Short-term self-soothing and staying alert, escaping fatigue and Anxiety, maintaining a sense of task execution
target_behavior.consequence: Weight gain, Decreased self-esteem, affected Relationships with friends, daily self-care and healthy habits disrupted
